Louisville appeared to be ready to make a charge with a close loss to Ole Miss, a great 41-31 win over SMU, and winnable games coming up. A 30-27 loss to Wake Forest and a 31-28 loss to NC State later, and now the Cardinals have to win to stay alive in the ACC race. Florida State was done. Head coach Mike Norvell was all but fired, and then everything flipped. The Seminoles tuned up against Central Arkansas, and then stunned Virginia 38-7. Win this, and the season narrative totally changes. Florida State vs Louisville Quick Hits Florida State is on the road for four games in the next five, with a trip to Miami up next before hosting Clemson. Louisville goes to Syracuse next to start a run of three road games in four dates. Before the last meeting in the 2023 ACC Championship, the two teams split the previous ten games. The defense pitched one of its best games in a long time, considering the circumstances, holding the Cavalier passing game in check with a monstrous day from the pass rush. The Noles generated ten sacks and 12 tackles for loss. The relentless pressure should continue against a Louisville offensive front that's having a problem keeping teams out of the backfield. Why Louisville Will Win Can Florida State show up on the road? It's not quite fair to dog the Noles for losing at Alabama, but the program has lost 13 straight games outside of Tallahassee, going back to the win over Florida late in 2023. Louisville has to take a deep breath after the NC State loss. It played well. The ground game was great, quarterback Lincoln Kienholz was fine on his dinged up ankle, and everything was fine outside of three lost fumbles. Florida State hasn't forced a takeaway in a month. Florida State vs Louisville Prediction, Betting Lines Florida State isn't awful. The pieces are there – the ground game is solid, and look out if that pass rush keeps on rolling – but they have a hard time always fitting together. The Seminoles will crank up plenty of yards and points – the Louisville defense isn't anything special – but the offense will stall a few too many times, and the Cardinals will find their offensive scoring punch after two straight disappointments. away.blurb: Florida State linebacker Noah LaVallee was downgraded from probable to out after there was previously hope he would play in Week 5. The Seminoles will be without four linebackers after the LaVallee announcement, as the freshman will join Izayia Williams, Blake Nichelson, and Daylen Green on the sidelines this week. Noah's brother and fellow linebacker, Caleb, is currently listed as probable for the upcoming game. Florida State's linebacker depth just took another hit with Noah LaVallee downgraded to out for Week 5 Florida State entered the game with a handful of players already confirmed to be out of the Week 5 game, but losing LaVallee particularly stings since he is a player filling in due to the injuries. LaVallee did not record any stats through the first three games, but began to work into the rotation against Central Arkansas with 21 snaps. The injury list is still rather long, even with a handful of players removed. Defensive back Quindarrius Jones and Caleb LaVallee are still listed as probable for the upcoming game against Virginia. Florida State and Virginia both released lengthy injury reports ahead of the Week 5 battle on Saturday. Both teams will be without a good chunk of the roster, but the key difference is that the Seminoles will be without multiple players at a vital position, and another player from the same position just joined that list. 2026 has not been the most productive season up to this point for Florida State, with a handful of players powering through bumps and bruises to compensate for the number of more serious injuries, particularly on defense. Starting safety Ashlynd Barker has been playing through a broken bone in his arm, although somewhat controversially , to make up for the shocking injury total. Without Noah and potentially Caleb in the picture, the slack will need to be picked up by the likes of Karon Maycock and AJ Cottrill. Maycock, a freshman, saw his first real action of the season against Central Arkansas and recorded three total tackles. Cottrill, on the other hand, saw action against SMU and Central Arkansas, totaling two tackles. During the Week 3 game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa, Florida State only played four linebackers and opted to use plenty of defensive backs. With Mikai Gbayor, Chris Jones, and Omar Graham Jr. all expected to play in Week 5, the Seminoles' staff might just give the remaining snaps at linebacker to the more experienced Cottrill. The only issue, however, is that Alabama and Virginia are far different teams in terms of how the offense attacks opposing defenses. Virginia is going to look to keep the football on the ground for most of the game. When combined with the play-action heavy passing attack, the Seminoles' linebackers could tire easily, which will force more of the remaining depth into the game. away.blurb: Florida State and Louisville have released their initial injury reports ahead of Friday night's clash, according to Yahoo Sports . The Seminoles are without key receivers and defensive backs, while the Cardinals have their starting quarterback listed as probable. This report matters because it tells you exactly who will step onto the field when the teams meet at 7 PM on ESPN. Fans need to know the starting lineup before the game starts. The Seminoles are dealing with a long list of players who will not be available. Running back Samuel Singleton Jr. is out, along with wide receiver Devin Carter. The team is missing several other players on the defensive side of the ball, including Daylen Green and Noah LaVallee. These absences force coach Mike Norvell to shuffle his depth chart significantly before kickoff. On the positive side, linebacker Mikai Gbayor and Karon Maycock are probable. Defensive back Antonio Cromartie Jr. and punter Daniel Hughes are also expected to play. However, defensive lineman Darryll Desir is questionable after not playing last week. picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska is getting ready for a huge Big Ten matchup against Indiana, and Adam Carriker breaks down what the Huskers have to do if they want to pull off the upset and earn some serious respect. This is one of those games that can change the way people look at a team. Nebraska has put together a strong start, but now the Huskers get a chance to prove it against a ranked Indiana team led by Curt Cignetti. Indiana has been one of the best teams in the Big Ten, and this game will give Matt Rhule’s team a chance to show how far it has come. Carriker starts by looking back at the history between Nebraska and Indiana; he then shifts to Nebraska’s offense and quarterback Anthony Colandrea. If Nebraska is going to win this game, Colandrea will need to have a big day. He has to make smart decisions, take care of the football, and make plays with both his arm and his legs. Carriker also compares Colandrea to Indiana’s quarterback Josh Hoover and talks about why Nebraska needs to put pressure on Hoover and force him into mistakes. The Huskers’ pass catchers are another major part of the matchup. Nebraska has playmakers who can make a difference, and Carriker takes a closer look at players like Kwazi Gilmer and how they match up with Indiana’s defense. On the other side of the ball, Nebraska’s defense could be one of the biggest factors in the game. Rob Aurich and the Nebraska defense will need to be at their best, especially on third down. Indiana has talented receivers, solid running backs, and an offense that can hurt teams in several different ways. Nebraska cannot afford to give up easy conversions or big plays. One of the biggest topics in the episode is penalties. Nebraska had 16 penalties last week while Indiana had zero. That is a massive difference, and Carriker makes it clear that Nebraska cannot expect to beat a ranked team if it keeps hurting itself. Cleaning up the penalties is one of his biggest keys to the game. Carriker wraps up the show by laying out five keys for Nebraska: limit penalties, stop the run, play four full quarters, run the football, and limit big plays. None of those things are complicated, but Nebraska has to do all five if it wants to compete and win. The Huskers also need to be ready for a physical game. Carriker talks about trading blows with Indiana and matching the Hoosiers for all four quarters. This cannot be a game where Nebraska plays well for two or three quarters and then fades late. The second half will be huge. Carriker also throws in a little extra motivation with a beard bet if Nebraska wins. At the end of the show, he gives his final score prediction: Indiana 27, Nebraska 24. He sees it as a close game, but Nebraska will need a big performance from Colandrea, a strong game from the defense, and much cleaner football to pull off the upset. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. That won't be good enough against the Huskers' biggest test yet: the undefeated, defending national champions from Indiana . Rob Aurich knows it, too, and the Huskers' defensive coordinator says Saturday's contest will be decided by how well NU handles the little things, from players doing their jobs to tackling at a high level. I thought two weeks ago we ran to the ball harder than we did last week. I was disappointed in that. I want people to talk about our defense as the hardest-playing group in the country. So, we’ve got to play extremely hard.” “The backs have a high break tackle ratio,” he continued. “We’ve got to tackle their backs at an elite level, which is something we’re going to work on today.” Anthony Jones Jr. makes a tackle against Michigan State. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Huskers allowed several explosive plays against the Terrapins last week, which is a major concern heading into a matchup against the likes of Indiana. And the Cornhuskers are off to a good start, coming in undefeated through five games, but still unranked and beating teams that are nothing like the caliber of opponent that they'll see this weekend in the Hoosiers and their 21-game win streak. What do experts think of this week's matchup? For that, let's turn to the SP+ college football model to project the outcome, and use it to lock in our own prediction. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Indiana remains the expected favorite against Nebraska on the road, but in what could be a close game. SP+ predicts that Indiana will defeat Nebraska by a projected score of 31 to 24 and will win the game by an expected margin of 7.7 points on the road. The model gives the Hoosiers a strong 69 percent chance of outright victory. SP+ is a "tempo- and opponent-adjusted measure of college football efficiency" that attempts to predict game outcomes by measuring "the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football." How good is it this season? So far, the SP+ college football prediction model is 146-122-3 in its picks against the spread with a 54.4 win percentage. What actually happens? Can the Huskers catch the Hoosiers? There's a lot to like about the Cornhuskers' offense right now. It ranks top 15 in points per game, scoring at least 31 in every game, and 48 in three out of five outings. Indiana hasn't looked its usual self until laying a 47-15 beating on Rutgers a week ago, and it still boasts one of the most potent rushing attacks in the country, tacking on 253 yards on the ground on average. Nebraska has performed admirably well against its competition thus far, but the discrepancy between what the Hoosiers put on the field compared to those other teams is too great to ignore. Home field keeps the Huskers in it for a while, but Indiana has the firepower to pull away by double digits. What happens? Indiana beats Nebraska and covers the spread. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images thehooch36 Mon, October 5, 2026 at 1:29 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College Football can be odd. One minute, you're winning your conference opener on the road 31-13. The next minute, you're winning you're conference home opener 48-25. You don't look particularly great in either contest, but you cover the spread, hold up your end of the bargain, and sit 5-0 to start the year for the first time since 2016. That's the story of the Nebraska Cornhuskers. LINCOLN, NE - OCTOBER 3: Nebraska defensive back Jeremiah Charles (25) celebrates after blocking a punt in the first quarter of the game between the Maryland Terrapins and the Nebraska Cornhuskers on October 3, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln, NE. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Nebraska took care of the Maryland Terrapins, albeit with one of the more dysfunctional beginnings to a game you'll see. A penalty on a (nearly) blocked punt that extended Maryland's drive, resulting in a field goal. Then after a three-and-out, an actual blocked punt that resulted in a Mekhi Nelson touchdown, his first of two in the game. Nebraska trained as much as 16-7, but still led 28-23 heading into halftime. The third quarter was a checkers match of moving a piece at a time, far away from your opponent. But the Huskers scored two seconds into the fourth quarter, and added two more touchdowns before the game ended. Meanwhile, the Nebraska defense held the Terps scoreless and relatively impotent after the 8:54 mark of the second quarter. Now it is time for the Huskers' biggest (and some may say first true) test of the season when the defending national champion Indiana Hoosiers make their way to Lincoln for Fox's Big Noon Kickoff. Curt Cignetti has his team in the top ten (top five in the Coaches' Poll), and even though there's no Fernando Mendoza, the Hoosiers are the only other team in the Bin ten to be undefeated. They have only been threatened once this year, when the Northwestern Wildcats of all teams gave them a scare, as the Hoosiers won that September 25 contest 29-23 at home. Indiana handled Rutgers this past weekend, and they mowed through their non-conference opponents (North Texas, Howard, and Western Kentucky) on easy mode. How will Nebraska perform against a rated team? Can they break the streak and knock off a ranked opponent? Would the rebuild fully be "on" if such a feat were to occur? Regardless of our collective thoughts on the outcome of the game, Vegas isn't counting on it. The line on FanDuel Sportsbook has Indiana as a 7.5-point favorite, marking the first time this season that Nebraska entered as the underdog. The over/under for the contest is 52.5 points. Bet your heart, but do so responsibly. Big Noon Kickoff between Nebraska and Indiana is Saturday at 11:00am Central, LIVE from Memorial Stadium, on Fox!

picks.blurb: Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction: The Huskers' Big Moment - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers return to NLCS Rays sweep Yankees Brewers clinch NLCS Valkyries, Dream win Game 2s NFL Power Rankings Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction: The Huskers' Big Moment Pete Fiutak Wed, October 7, 2026 at 6:51 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Nebraska enjoyed a few terrific seasons over the last 25 years, but for all intents and purposes, the historic superpower hasn't been in the national title hunt since losing to Miami in the BCS Championship to end the 2001 season. There's still plenty of work to do after this week, but beating the defending national champion – and putting an end to Indiana's 21-game winning streak – would be just the moment the program has been waiting for to show that it's headed in the right direction. Indiana hasn't been the dominant version of last year, but it's still unbeaten, it's about as tuned up as it can be, and it got its first road game out of the way with a 47-15 win over Rutgers. Yeah, this might be Nebraska's moment. It's also Curt Cignetti's moment to prove that for the Hoosiers, it's business as usual. Indiana vs Nebraska Quick Hits The Hoosiers get three home games in the next four after this, but Ohio State is up next, the road date is at Michigan, and then Minnesota and USC come to Bloomington. Nebraska goes on the road for three games in the next four dates, with a trip to Oregon before a week off to get ready for Washington. Indiana won 56-7 in 2024, but the Huskers are 6-1 in the series before that going back to a Hoosier win in 1959. How To Watch Indiana vs Nebraska Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Memorial Stadium, Lincoln, NE – Week 6 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 6 Why Indiana Will Win As you'd expect from one of the best coached teams in all of sports, Indiana doesn't mess up. It has only turned the ball over once, it's third in the nation in fewest penalties, and no one does a better job of not putting itself in tough situations. It might not be that Nebraska needs to force mistakes and can win this straight up, but it has a way of pulling away in games, helped by the takeaways. On the flip side, the Huskers were flagged 16 times in the win over Maryland and have committed the most penalties of any Big Ten team so far. Why Nebraska Will Win The Hoosiers have only been stress-tested once in the 29-23 win over Northwestern, and that was partly because Wildcat quarterback Aidan Chiles was accurate with the passing game. Nebraska's Anthony Colandrea might not be Drew Brees, but he's hitting 66% of his passes with 13 touchdowns and just two picks. This has to be about the Nebraska offensive line, though. The Huskers are taking over games with the running game pushing until the dam breaks, and then games turn into routs. Indiana isn't Maryland or Bowling Green, but Michigan State is a tough-as-nails team that was the only team that held the Huskers to under 200 yards, and it still lost by 18. Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction, Betting Lines Can Nebraska get close to 40 carries? Part of the problem against Indiana is that teams have to give up on the run because it doesn't work. Only North Texas has been able to get past 66 yards this season, and it's also the only team that ran more than 35 times. North Texas also lost 52-16. The energy of the moment will carry the Huskers to a solid first half, but they won't be able to pull away. Eventually, the Nebraska run defense will start to buckle, the IU pass rush will get to Colandrea, and the hype for the Ohio State game will start about 30 seconds after the final gun. away.headline: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers
away.blurb: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers Skip to main content SI.COM Indiana could be without its leading rusher Saturday night when the Hoosiers take on Rutgers, with running back Lee Beebe Jr. listed as a game-time decision, per the Big Ten's availability report . Beebe, who rushed for 203 yards in Indiana's win over Northwestern last week, was a midweek addition to the availability report. His status headlines an otherwise encouraging final injury update for the Hoosiers, who had three players removed from the report ahead of their first road test of the season. Richard was listed as probable Friday before being removed from Saturday's report, putting him in line to handle the bulk of Indiana's rushing workload should Beebe be unable to go. Cuono, a second-year depth running back with 11 carries for 45 yards this season, would likely serve as Richard's primary backup in that scenario. True freshman Jayreon Campbell, who has rushed six times for 43 yards in limited action, is also available. Khobie Martin, meanwhile, remains out for the fourth consecutive game as he continues recovering from a forearm injury he suffered in Indiana's season opener against North Texas. Martin is expected to return around the midway point of the season. Indiana enters Saturday with a rushing attack ranked among the nation's top 10, although Beebe's potential absence would leave the Hoosiers without one of their most productive offensive weapons. Linebacker Rolijah Hardy, who was listed as probable Friday after suffering an injury late in his eight-tackle performance against Northwestern, was also removed from Saturday's availability report and is expected to play. A.J. Harris, Daniel Ndukwe among those ruled out Defensive end Daniel Ndukwe is also out, marking his first absence of the season. Ndukwe ranks second on the team with 4.5 tackles for loss, including 1.5 against Northwestern last week. Indiana still has considerable depth at edge, with Stephen Daley, Kellan Wyatt, Tobi Osunsanmi, Chiddi Obiazor and Josh Burnham available to help absorb his absence. Elsewhere, cornerback Carson Williams and wide receiver Lebron Bond remain out for the third and fourth consecutive games, respectively. Indiana and Rutgers are scheduled to kick off at 8 p.m. ET. His return would bolster a running back room with an alarmingly low amount of career production. After being upgraded from questionable to probable, he appears set to return against the Terps. That would give the Huskers a key piece in both their passing and return games. If he sits this one out, more catches could be in store for Quinn Clark and Keelan Smith. Isaiah Mozee and Andrew Marshall are options as punt returners. The surprising news came Thursday when junior running back Mekhi Nelson was added to the availability report as questionable. That status stayed the same on Friday. Nelson's availability would provide a significant boost for the Huskers on the ground against Maryland. picks.headline: West Virginia football expert previews the Arizona game, makes a score prediction
picks.blurb: West Virginia football expert previews the Arizona game, makes a score prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers return to NLCS Rays sweep Yankees Brewers clinch NLCS Valkyries, Dream win Game 2s NFL Power Rankings AMES, IA - OCTOBER 3: Head coach Rich Rodriguez of the West Virginia Mountaineers shakes hands with quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. #3 of the West Virginia Mountaineers celebrating a Mountaineers touchdown in the first half of play against the Iowa State Cyclones at Jack Trice Stadium on October 3, 2026, in Ames, Iowa. (Photo by David Purdy/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brian Pedersen Tue, October 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's not just Game Week, it's RichRod Game Week! Arizona's first trip to West Virginia will see it face off against former head coach Rich Rodriguez , who is back with the Mountaineers for a second go-around. Rodriguez coached there from 2001-07 before going to Michigan for three years and then spending 2012-17 with the Wildcats. The current West Virginia team is on a 2-game skid, losing a 45-42 shootout at Iowa State last weekend after falling at home to Oklahoma State in its Big 12 opener. To better understand RichRod's squad, we reached out to Dillon Clark of SB Nation sister site The Smoking Musket for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his impressive answers to our mediocre questions: AZ Desert Swarm: West Virginia went 3-0 in nonconference play, including an impressive win over Virginia, but then has lost both conference games. What have been the main contributing factors to the backslide? Dillon Clark: "There has been a significant increase in competition in Big 12 play compared to our nonconference schedule. The win against Virginia looked good at the time because they were ranked, but after their performance against Florida State last week I don't think they are going to be anywhere near the top of the ACC again. Our defense hasn't looked great all year but the wheels have come completely off in the last two games. We have given up over 1,200 yards of total offense in the last two games which equates to about 3/4 of a mile if you were wondering." It's to no one's surprise in Wildcat Nation that a RichRod-coached team is running the ball well, but this production seems to be at another level. What's been the key to the rushing success, and how do you think Arizona's defense will try to neutralize this? "We spent a ton of money in the portal on a quarterback, running back and several offensive linemen. Michael Hawkins Jr. has exceeded expectations at the quarterback position for us averaging over 100 yards per game on the ground 6.2 yards per carry. Many of his best runs are coming off of pass plays that would have resulted in a sack or throw away for most other QBs so when you turn those negative plays into big positives it really shows up on the stat sheet. One of the biggest surprises to me has been his elusiveness in the red zone and the ability to make people miss. I knew he was fast, I didn't realize how shifty he is. Cam Cook has also produced at a high level in the RB position. He is such a tough runner. His yards after contact and broken tackles are what really sets him apart. Even though he isn't what I would call fast, he has consistently popped big runs. He gets stronger as the game goes on and the majority of his yardage has come in the second half of games." Quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. is tied for the FBS lead with 11 rushing touchdowns, but how is he as a passer? Would you trust him if he had to be one-dimensional in this way? "I think it's fair to call Michael Hawkins Jr. a streaky passer. The last three games he has started out looking a bit shaky in the pass game with off target throws. In two of the three he eventually settled in and made plays with his arm. The completion percentage against Iowa State was a bit lower than you like, but he did have a couple drops and throw aways in there. I have confidence in him as a passer, my bigger question is can our receivers get open consistently in a situation where we have to throw the ball, and can we establish an intermediate passing game? It feels like our passing game at times this year has been all or nothing. The drive-extending, possession-style passing game has not been sharp. I don't blame that on Michael Hawkins as much as I do on play calling and scheme. I have a hard time seeing anyone making him purely one dimensional as a passer this year. Teams may shut down our traditional running game, but we have seen teams put multiple spies on him in the past few weeks and he is still escaping the pocket for chunk yardage." The Mountaineers' defensive numbers are not good, ranking last in the Big 12 in almost every category. Is this a talent issue, a problem with the scheme, or both? "In order to be as bad as we have been, it has to be all of the above right? Our tackling is bad. Missed assignments on nearly every possession.We can't get pressure on the quarterback. When we are in the right place we end up with a pass interference penalty. It's rough all around. There has been a lot of talk on if Zac Alley's reputation as a sort of 'mad scientist' on defense could be part of the problem. It's really hard to argue against that when you see us consistently confused on pre-snap alignments. The biggest concern is that we are struggling in every aspect. Scoring defense, rushing defense, pass defense, total yardage, it doesn't matter which stat you look at, we are at or near the bottom. The only hope is that potentially our two best defenders just became eligible last week. Jacorey Thomas and Jason Chambers should help plug some holes in what has been a leaky secondary. There is only one way for us to go from here." How has the second coming of RichRod been so far in your estimation? Have there been any classic moments in terms of his antics? "After the Virginia win in Week 3 the vibes around the WVU fan base were as high as I've seen them in a very long time. That game brought back a lot of great memories from Rich Rod's first tenure here and it felt like the sky was the limit. The last two weeks have put a damper on the mood though the fact that the offense has been producing at a high level still does take some of the blame off of him. The Rich Rod offense is back and it's humming, but how did he not see this coming with the defense? There was definitely a group of the fanbase that didn't want him back, and those voices are getting louder with each loss. I think he has shown enough so far that the majority of the fan base still believes he can get this right. We love that he holds players accountable in the moment, and it gives us hope that he can turn this thing around." Prediction time. Does Arizona beat its former coach and get a big conference road win or do the Mountaineers hold serve at home? Give us a score prediction. "We have the worst defense in the Big 12. You have one of the best offenses. We are coming off of two straight brutal conference losses. You are coming off of a dominant win against a previously undefeated Cincinnati team. In other words, we have you right where we want you. 45-31 Mountaineers get back on track at home."

picks.blurb: Arizona vs. West Virginia Prediction, Pick and Odds for Week 6 Teams Arizona Wildcats Arizona State Sun Devils Cincinnati Bearcats Colorado Buffaloes Houston Cougars Iowa State Cyclones Kansas Jayhawks Kansas State Wildcats Oklahoma State Cowboys TCU Horned Frogs Texas Tech Red Raiders West Virginia Mountaineers Former Foes Missouri Tigers Nebraska Cornhuskers Oklahoma Sooners Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Recruiting Football Transfer Portal Video Watch on YouTube Listen on Apple Listen on Spotify Forum Members Login Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today Arizona hits the road in Week 6 for a trip to Morgantown, where the Wildcats will take on West Virginia in an intriguing Big 12 matchup at Milan Puskar Stadium. The Wildcats enter Saturday at 4-1 overall and 1-1 in Big 12 play after making a major statement with a 34-7 win over previously unbeaten Cincinnati. West Virginia, meanwhile, is 3-2 overall and still searching for its first conference victory after dropping back-to-back games against Oklahoma State and Iowa State. The Mountaineers' latest loss was a wild 45-42 shootout in Ames. There's also an obvious storyline on the West Virginia sideline, where former Arizona head coach Rich Rodriguez will face his old program. Rodriguez coached the Wildcats from 2012-17 before eventually returning to Morgantown for his second stint leading the Mountaineers. Can Arizona build off its impressive win over Cincinnati, or will West Virginia get its first Big 12 victory of the season at home? Here's everything you need to know about Arizona vs. West Virginia , including the latest odds, our biggest question and our prediction and pick for Saturday's Week 6 matchup. West Virginia vs. Arizona Odds Spread: Arizona -3.5 Over/Under: 61.5 Moneyline: Arizona -162/West Virginia +134 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: Can West Virginia's Defense Stop Anything? This West Virginia defense is just horrible. They gave up 577 yards to Iowa State last week, and are allowing a Big 12-worst 456 yards per game, which is 50 more yards per game than any other Big 12 team. They're dead last in passing and rushing yards allowed per game, and second-worst in points allowed per game. The Mountaineers are 100th in the nation in net yards per play (offense minus defense), and rank dead last in defensive efficiency in the league. OK, you get the point. So what is Rich Rodriguez and Zac Alley changing ahead of Saturday? It's not clear. But something needs to change. West Virginia vs. Arizona Prediction and Pick Prediction: Arizona 35, West Virginia 31 The West Virginia Mountaineers are going to be desperate to avoid an 0-3 start in Big 12 play. They have the running game to keep this thing competitive, however, Arizona's front seven is underrated. One week after Cincinnati rushed for over 200 yards vs. Kansas State, they only mustered 74 yards on 28 carries for 2.6 yards per carry vs. Arizona. I don't believe Arizona will have that level of success vs. this WVU rushing attack, that has been the most-potent in the Big 12, but they'll do enough. And if Arizona can jump out to a lead and force Michael Hawkins Jr. to try and win a game through the air, that's a recipe for success. The only concern I have for Arizona is the travel and early kick at 12:00 p.m. CT, which will be a 9:00 a.m. kick for Arizona's body clock. Those games are always tough. However, if you're worried you're on an island with Arizona, don't be. The Wildcats are attracting 91% of the money wagered and have been bet up from -3 to -3.5 , indicating that both recreational and larger bettors are backing Arizona. Sometimes the obvious side is obvious for a reason. Arizona wins. Arizona covers. The Arizona Wildcats will be without one of their top wide receivers this season. Arizona senior receiver Tre Spivey suffered a broken foot on the Wildcats' final possession of the first half in Saturday's 34-7 win over Cincinnati. Spivey, who watched the final two quarters of Arizona's win over Cincinnati in a walking boot and crutch, is expected to miss the remainder of the season. Former Oklahoma, Houston and Tarleton State player Cody Jackson erupted for 160 receiving yards in the Cyclones’ momentum swing-filled 45-42 triumph over West Virginia at Jack Trice Stadium. Oct 3, 2026 Updated Oct 3, 2026 AMES — Cody Jackson transferred to Iowa State last winter in search of his fourth fresh start. The talented transfer wide receiver found it, but catches proved tough to come by. Until Saturday, when the former Oklahoma, Houston and Tarleton State player erupted for 160 receiving yards in the Cyclones’ momentum swing-filled 45-42 triumph over West Virginia at Jack Trice Stadium. “I trusted in God, number one, and trusted in my coaches (and) my teammates,” said Jackson, who didn’t record a catch in ISU’s first two games, but now has 12 receptions in the past two games. “Not having my head down. Keeping my head high. Keeping a smile on my face every day and coming in and working at practice.” Jackson’s first grab on Saturday for the Cyclones (3-2, 1-1 Big 12) turned into a 46-yard touchdown on a halfback toss from Aiden Flora. His other seven receptions against the Mountaineers (3-3, 0-2) came during a tense second half, and many fueled three straight scoring drives that helped ISU preserve the win. “He did a great job finding open windows and attacking the ball in the air,” Cyclones quarterback Jaylen Raynor said. Jackson notched 92 yards after the catch and often adjusted his routes as Raynor improvised amid amped up West Virginia pressure. His 43-yard catch on third-and-six early in the fourth quarter set up Kyle Konrardy’s 35-yard field goal that gave ISU a 31-28 lead. And Jackson’s 15-yard grab on the Cyclones’ final scoring drive ended in one of Flora’s three rushing touchdowns. Flora’s now averaging 8.1 yards per carry and has rushed for 600 yards and six touchdowns. “(He’s) a great leader,” Jackson said. “He can do everything, like you could see. away.headline: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense
away.blurb: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense As they practiced on Tuesday for game prep coming off their bye week, Green Wave running back Jamauri McClure was a sight for sore eyes out there, participating in team drills without a non-contact jersey for the first time since he went down with a fractured foot in fall camp. This year's room looks a lot different in comparison. Maurice Turner is playing his best football right now. Jaylin Lucas has gotten some work out in space a bit more this week of prep. Johnnie Daniels has shown that he can throw a killer block as much as he can shoot through a gap. However, the return of McClure is what fans have been clamoring for since the news first got out that he was hurt. Now that he's had ample time to recover, his return should be a major boost for a Tulane offense looking to make the most out of and stretch out what should be expected to be limited possessions against the Army Black Knights Saturday. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Maddy Hudak Tue, October 6, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The best ability is often availability, and the Tulane Green Wave certainly have some good news on that front ahead of American conference play. But while head coach Will Hall told media members on Tuesday that he and the team feel that they're a better football team than when we last talked to and saw them last two weeks back, they have a lot to prove on the road to kick off their conference slate. An essential thing they're looking for is an identity on offense. Well, a lot of that can be solved by a strong rush attack that McClure instantaneously boosts. When McClure started taking over the starting running back job towards the end of the year last season, it was clear that he had a different gear and set of traits than what we were seeing from that room. Further good news on that front is that nothing appears to be up with Turner, who ended up limping a bit at the end of his 74-yard touchdown run against the Southern Miss Golden Eagles, as he also was practicing in full with no non-contact jersey. But the true finesse of that room lies with McClure. Another major returnee was wide receiver Zycarl Lewis, who got injured during the season opener against the Duke Blue Devils and hasn't practiced or played since. He was also not in a non-contact jersey on the practice field Tuesday. McClure averaged an impressive 6.5 yards per carry last season. The redshirt sophomore had eight total carries until Week 12 of last year against the FAU Owls. In the final five games of the season, he added 75 touches for 83 total carries for 540 yards and two touchdowns.

away.headline: Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane
away.blurb: News Sports Life Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLLEGE Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane Ken McMillan Middletown Times Herald- Record Updated Oct. 6, 2026, 9:47 a.m. ET In the end, Army's 21-19 loss at Louisiana Tech on Saturday night was just a non-conference game and didn't affect the American Conference standings. However, the Black Knights are having trouble building on positives. "It's very hard to play perfect,'' said Monken, who also points out the margin for error is slim for his West Point teams. "We're going to strive to it.'' Monken pointed out that Army had too many missed assignments, played with poor fundamentals at times and didn't help themselves with six penalties, but he's not given up on the squad. A dominant win over Bryant in the opener, followed by a crushing late loss at home to South Florida. A tough road win over Temple, followed by a stumbling loss as a small favorite at Louisiana Tech , dropping the Black Knights to 2-2. "We're not going to let this game kind of derail our season,'' said senior center and co-captain Brady Small. "We're going to go back, we're going to watch some film, we're going to learn and get ready for Tulane, another conference game. So just use this as fuel to the fire to get us a win at home.'' Army is a three-point favorite over Tulane for Saturday's noon ET start. Army is 1-1 in American action, and needs a win vs. the Green Wave to stay in contact with the 1-0 leaders: Florida Atlantic (4-1 overall), Memphis (4-1), Texas San Antonio (4-1), Alabama Birmingham (3-2) and North Texas (3-2). Army will face FAU and Memphis but not the other three this season. "Honestly, we've just got to attack the adversity at hand,'' said back Samari Howard. "We can't let this be a lull in our preparation. Overall, we've got to come together as a collective and tackle the adversity and get ready for the next week and the week after that.'' "I don't believe anybody loses momentum unless they stop believing,'' head coach Jeff Monken said. "And I don't think our guys will stop believing. ... If we allow it to derail us, then shame on us. Weve got to learn from it, and each game is independent of the last one. I don't think we allowed last week (win over Temple) to linger into this week. We weren't patting ourselves on the back for such a great job.'' Monken always reminds people that winning college football games is hard. "I love our team,'' he said. "They're tough as nails. They compete, and we played all the way to the end tonight.'' West Point and New Orleans are separated by more than 1,300 miles, but the football programs at Army and Tulane remain very familiar. The Green Wave have a long history with the Black Knights, dating back to 1953 when the two schools battled to a scoreless draw. Next to service academy rivals Navy and Air Force, Army and Tulane have met quite often, 21 times since 1996. Tulane was a founding member of Conference USA in 199

picks.blurb: ‘This game is almost always close' – National media outlet predicts the final score of Oklahoma vs Texas - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers return to NLCS Rays sweep Yankees Brewers clinch NLCS Valkyries, Dream win Game 2s NFL Power Rankings BRYAN TERRY/THE OKLAHOMAN / USA TODAY NETWORK Zach Ragan Wed, October 7, 2026 at 4:37 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oklahoma Sooners and the Texas Longhorns will meet in Dallas. The Texas Longhorns and Oklahoma Sooners will meet in Dallas this weekend for a huge SEC showdown. Texas has won three of the last four games in this rivalry after losing four straight from 2018 to 2021. The Longhorns are having the better season, and they have the better roster, but the result of this game has been close in some years when it shouldn't have been. CBS Sports' Chris Hummer and Brad Crawford made their predictions for the game, and they have Texas winning. Hummer has the Longhorns winning 20-17. "Historically, this game is almost always close," wrote Hummer. "Nine of the last 14 regular-season matchups were decided by a possession or fewer. I haven't seen anything so far this year that makes me feel differently about this game. I have more faith in Texas than Oklahoma. … At the risk of far oversimplifying a complicated game, I feel very confident in saying the QB who plays best, be it Texas' Arch Manning or Oklahoma's John Mateer, will win this game. I have slightly more faith in Manning at this point, so give me the Longhorns to win in a close one." Crawford, meanwhile, has Texas winning 24-14. "I just can't envision a reality in which Oklahoma scores enough points with this offense against Will Muschamp to warrant picking the cover here," noted Crawford. "Even with an extra week to sort out the struggles with the passing game under John Mateer, this Oklahoma team plays with little confidence when it has the football, and that means something against the No. 1 team in the country, hoping to tee off on the quarterback." Oklahoma vs Texas will kick off at 2:30 PM CT/3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ABC. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.headline: 2026 Texas Longhorns - Oklahoma Sooners Preview: Oklahomeless Offense
No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma preview: Reeling Sooners look to pull off upset
picks.blurb: No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma preview: Reeling Sooners look to pull off upset | Burnt Orange Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Texas Longhorns Community Burnt Orange Nation October 8, 2026 Burnt Orange Nation Notifications Notifications Get The App Sections Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Texas Football Odds Texas Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search Get The App Sections Expand Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications Texas Longhorns Football The Sooners head to Dallas with a struggling offense and stingy defense. Fresh off a bye week with a 4-0 record, the No. 1 Texas Longhorns head up I-35 for the annual Red River Rivalry against the Oklahoma Sooners, who have struggled thus far in 2026 — Oklahoma has a 2-2 record on the year and has failed to score more than 14 points in each of their last three contests. On paper, this is a matchup that should favor the Longhorns, but if history has shown anything, nothing matters once these two teams take the field at the Cotton Bowl. Scoring points against the Oklahoma defense is doable but will undoubtedly be the biggest challenge facing the Longhorns. “This is always a unique game because you can take record, stats, and all those things and throw them out the window,” Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said on Monday. “You’ve got to play the game and you’ve got to play the game the right way.” The struggles for the Sooners start on the offensive end. Returning quarterback John Mateer has failed to effectively move the ball through the air and the running attack ranks 131st in the FBS in yards per game. Second-year offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle has made his money with Mateer at the helm, a partnership that is now in it’s fourth year and dates back to their time together at Washington State, but is currently testing the patience of Oklahoma fans given the offense’s lack of scoring. “Coach Venables, I know he’s probably sitting there thinking he wishes the record was a little bit different, but man, his teams play hard, and this team’s no different,” Sarkisian said. “They play hard. They’re an excellent defensive football team. They’ve got draft picks all over on the defense. Offensively, they’ve got playmaking ability similar to us. They’re trying to find their way to to find that level of consistency. But one thing I can be assured of — we’re going to get their best shot, and so I think it’s important for us that we focus on what we need to do so that we can play our best football.” With concerns across the Sooner offense, this year’s rendition will likely be determined by the success of the Longhorns finding the end zone in the Cotton Bowl. If the Longhorns can score points, things could get out of hand. Here’s what to expect on Saturday. As mentioned, the Oklahoma offense is headed by Arbuckle and Mateer. Arbuckle is a young and forward-thinking coordinator with a track record of quarterback development and roots in the Air Raid. At 31 years old, he has already helped develop Bailey Zappe, Austin Reed, and Cam Ward. His offense utilizes tempo and the run game to stretch defenses and create passing windows. With the athleticism of Mateer and the inability to create an impactful rushing attack otherwise, Arbuckle has adapted the offense to feature a quarterback run threat on nearly every play. Averaging just 22 points per game and coming off a bye week, a few new wrinkles are all but guaranteed from Arbuckle on Saturday. Much has been made of Mateer’s play at quarterback this season. The returning starter for the Sooners came into the season with lofty expectations after a turnover-prone 2025 season. Through four games, his play has been disappointing, prompting Venables to admit that he considered benching his starting quarterback at halftime of the Georgia loss. Mateer has completed 66.1 percent of his passes for 883 yards and eight touchdowns while adding 41 carries for 76 yards. However, Mateer has turned the ball over six times in four games, including three first-half turnovers last week against Georgia. Pro Football Focus has tracked eight throws by Mateer as turnover worthy this season. Holding on to the ball is priority number one for Mateer, who has looked rattled in the pocket the season. He’s missed reads, held on to the ball, and fired inaccurately on numerous occasions. Keeping Mateer uncomfortable sets the tone for the Texas defense. Nearly everything else is downstream of whether the Longhorn front can keep him guessing and rushed. Keeping Mateer’s legs out of the game will be another key for Texas — if Mateer can extend plays or effectively pick up first downs on designed runs, things get significantly more complicated for the Longhorn defense. Expect a heavy dose of quick, high-completion throws to start the game in order to neutralize the Texas pass rush and get Mateer into a rhythm. The lead back for the Sooners is junior Lloyd Avant. Avant is a 5’10, 212-pound ball carrier from Humble who has racked up 164 yards and a touchdown on 42 carries (3.9 YPC). A transfer from Colorado State, Avant was expected to compete for snaps with Tory Blaylock, but has been thrust into the starting role due to Blaylock’s hamstring injury. Against UTEP, Avant looked strong, rushing for 79 yards on 15 carries; however, in the three games since, he has carried the ball 27 times for just 85 yards. Blaylock came into the season as the leading back, but is recovering from injury. He’s gotten a handful of carries, but its clear that the coaching staff does have not believe he is close to 100 percent. With an additional week to recover, it’s very possible that he contributes in a more meaningful way on Saturday. Regardless of who takes handoffs, improvement is needed on the ground. After finishing 113th in rushing offense last season, the Sooners are 133rd in yards per rush and t-134th with two rushing touchdowns on the season. Despite an offseason of revamping the rushing attack, things have regressed through four games. “It’s frustrating because I feel like I’m not doing my part,” said tight end Rocky Beers , via OU Insider . “There’s always one miss here, one miss there, and it’s costing us... We’ve just got to believe in our blocks and hold onto them as long as we can.” Getting back to running the ball was undoubtedly a point of emphasis over the bye week and something that the Longhorns will need to thwart on Saturday. Wide receiver Perhaps the most talented player on the Sooner offense is leading wide receiver Isaiah Sategna. A transfer from Arkansas, Sategna leads the offense in receptions (20), yards (267), and longest play from scrimmage (53). His two touchdowns are tied for the most on the team. Listed at 5’10, Sategna isn’t a huge target but can be dangerous. His quickness can generate missed tackles and additional yardage after the catch, so closing in quickly will be important come Saturday. Sategna forced 22 missed tackles last season and half of his receiving yards this season have come after the catch. Transfers Trell Harris and Parker Livingstone were brought in to supplement Sategna but neither has been effective thus far. Harris remains sidelined with an injury and Livingstone hasn’t been able to make a difference, though this will undoubtedly be a big game for him after transferring from Texas during the offseason. Stopping Sategna will be the key to keeping the wide outs locked down, a task that Longhorns defensive coordinator Will Muschamp has to feel good about. Veteran tight end Rocky Beers, a Colorado State transfer, has proved to be a reliable weapon for Mateer in the passing game, tallying 18 catches for 255 yards and two touchdowns this season, which is the best on the team outside of Sategna. One of three tight ends brought in from the portal by new position coach Jason Witten, Beers has looked the part this season. His route running creates windows for Mateer and he has enough size to be a matchup problem on smaller defenders. When Oklahoma makes it to the red zone, Beers is a frequent target, something that Texas will need to take away come Saturday. Offensive line The running game has struggled for the Sooners and a big reason for that falls on the shoulders of the offensive line. This group has failed to keep a clean pocket, generate push, and open running lanes. If Oklahoma hopes to turn things around offensively, the five up front will need to step up their performance, immediately. Against Georgia, the Oklahoma offensive line switched things up, sitting Eddy Pierre-Louis at guard in favor of Heath Ozaeta and Noah Best, but it made little difference. E’Marion Harris, the right tackle, still looked a step slow while star left tackle Michael Fasusi remains sidelined with a shoulder injury. I’d expect this group to get additional help in blocking from tight ends and running backs, as well as a heavy dose of plays designed to get the ball out of Mateer’s hand quickly. This group has yet to show anything special through four games, increasing pressure on longtime position coach Bill Bedenbaugh, whose tenure dates to the Bob Stoops era. The Oklahoma offense has sputtered to start the year. Poor quarterback play coupled with a lack of rushing attack and porous offensive line has resulted in little points being scored. With a bye week to prepare for the Longhorns, I’d expect a sharpened game plan out of the gate that features quick passes and unique ways to get the ball out of Mateer’s hands. For the Longhorn defense to find success, getting pressure is key. When Mateer feels the pass rush, he has shown an inability to make good reads and deliver accurate passes. Keeping him from feeling comfortable will be a point of emphasis for the Longhorns. Outside of Mateer, limiting Sategna and Beers is the next priority. Forcing someone besides these three players to make a difference should spell success for the Longhorns. For every concern about the offense, the defense boasts a strength. This unit has been salty thanks to a solid crop of returners despite a mediocre offense on the other side of the ball that can’t finish drives and turns the ball over. Moving the ball through the air against the Sooners has been particularly tough. Allowing 122.5 passing yards per game, the OU secondary ranks fourth in the country, and is led by returning producers that understand the scheme and have the physical talent to implement it successfully. Opponents convert 23.1 percent of third downs, the third best in the entire country, meaning staying ahead of the chains will be essential for the Texas offense. The best method to attack this defense has been via the run. Averaging 115.5 yards per game on the ground and 3.23 yards per carry, this aspect remains in the top third of the country but lags behind the stellar pass and third-down defense. Don’t be mistaken by the record or score against Georgia — the Oklahoma defense can get after it. Defensive line Up front, there are four players that Texas will need to handle — defensive ends Taylor Wein and Adepoju Adebawore, and tackles David Stone and Jayden Jackson. In the middle, Stone and Jackson are a formidable duo. Stone was one of the Sooners’ most highly-regarded returners after notching 43 tackles a year ago. Now in his third year at Oklahoma, the 6’3, 312-pound lineman will be looking for his first win in Dallas. Next to him, Jackson is quite the player. Last season, he tallied 28 tackles and 3.0 sacks, including being honored as the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week for his performance against Auburn. This duo up front has been a big reason why the defense has been stout thus far. As of today, it has been 1,094 days since OU reached the end zone, dating back to the Sooners' 2023 upset (fluke) win over the Horns. However, even as Texas has held Oklahoma to just three field goals over the last two Red River Rivalries, the Longhorns haven't exactly put on offensive showcases . This year, the expectations for the offenses aren't all that different, and the oddsmakers have the 2026 Red River Rivalry as low-scoring as the last couple of seasons. But don't worry, they still have the Horns coming out on top. Early odds for No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma in Red River Rivalry Spread: -7.5 Texas, +7.5 Oklahoma Moneyline: -330 Texas, +260 Oklahoma Over/Under: +/-39.5 points While the oddsmakers have Texas walking away with a victory by more than a touchdown, they also have the point total set below 40 points between the two teams. In other words, they expect the final score to be somewhere around 23-16 or 24-16, seemingly alluding to the idea that the Sooners will be able to find the end zone in the Cotton Bowl, a first in nearly 1,100 days by the time the game kicks off on Saturday. The moneyline favors Texas a little more heavily, with someone having to bet $330 on the Horns just to profit $100, but only having to wager $100 on Oklahoma to walk away with a $260 profit. The Horns have allowed just 13.3 points per game so far this season, and that includes matchups against the then-No. 1 Ohio State Buckeyes and then-No. 14 Tennessee Volunteers. Meanwhile, in Oklahoma's only Power Conference games (losses to the then-unranked Michigan Wolverines and No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs), the Sooners have only averaged 11.5 points per game, and most of that is coming from the defense or special teams. Yes, the Horns obviously need to get the run game going again, but Manning's level of play seems to determine how well Texas performs on offense. By James Parks | October 7, 2026 One of college football’s great rivalry games renews this weekend as the Red River Shootout finds No. 1 ranked Texas facing off against Oklahoma in a critical test for both sides, if for very different reasons just a month into the 2026 season. Texas, still the class of the SEC , owns signature wins against Ohio State and Tennessee that catapulted it into the top AP ranking. Oklahoma fell out of the poll after falling to 2-2 and is once again facing structural questions around what remains a very anemic offense. What do the analytics department think of this week’s matchup? For that, let’s turn to the SP+ college football model to project the outcome, and use it to lock in our own prediction. Texas vs. Oklahoma score prediction: Can Arch Beat the Sooners' Defense? Sep 26, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) celebrates after a college football game between Tennessee and Texas at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn. on Sept. 26, 2026. Mandatory Credit: Brianna Paciorka-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) It may not come as a surprise that the Longhorns are getting the favorite treatment against the Sooners, and by a decent margin, too. SP+ predicts that Texas will defeat Oklahoma by a projected score of 27 to 17 and will win the game by an expected margin of 9.9 points in the process. The model gives the Longhorns a very strong 73 percent chance of victory, one of the biggest discrepancies of any game this weekend. SP+ is a “tempo- and opponent-adjusted measure of college football efficiency” that attempts to predict game outcomes by measuring “the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football.” How good is it this season? So far, the SP+ college football prediction model is 146-122-3 in its picks against the spread with a 54.4 win percentage. What actually happens? Can the Longhorns defend their No. 1 ranking? Sep 4, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) in action during the game against the UTEP Miners at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images That’s a different question. Even with a Texas win, its place atop the AP poll could be in danger anyway as pollsters may be more impressed with what happens between No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Alabama as they face off in primetime. A big win over the Sooners could sway enough voters to stay at No. 1 , and everything looks like it should go the Longhorns’ way. Even with questions around Arch Manning’s continued development at the quarterback position. Sure, Texas is 4-0 and Manning looks much better than this time last year, but he has also clearly still not performed to expectations, either. Arch is a decent 63 percent passer but is making some curious decisions and doesn’t look completely at ease in the pocket against better-quality fronts. Against an Oklahoma defense that, despite everything, remains one of college football’s best – 4th against the pass, top 25 in scoring, and 3rd in third-down conversions – Manning could get seriously rattled early. But the Longhorns still have an advantage of their own on defense. They have battery of elite pass rushers who can wreck OU’s blockers, shrink the pocket, and get at John Mateer on a regular basis. That should give the Texas offense enough chances to separate and pull away late. Horns by 10. What happens? Texas beats Oklahoma, and covers the spread. Texas gives injury non-update on Hollywood Smothers, Nick Townsend status once again Skip to main content Recruiting After nearly a week and a half since we last saw the Texas Longhorns take the field against the Tennessee Volunteers, many people were eager to hear how previously injured players had progressed over the bye. However, what should come as no surprise is that Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian had another idea in mind : no update. With star players like running back Hollywood Smothers, tight end Nick Townsend, and defensive lineman Justus Terry all missing time this season, Longhorn Nation has been eager to see their guys back in action. Unfortunately, we will have to wait to see what we should expect on Saturday. "I think we're healthier than we were a week ago at this time," Sarkisian said in his game preview press conference, continuing his refusal to share injury updates beyond what he puts in the SEC-mandated availability reports. Steve Sarkisian sticks to SEC availability report and nothing more On Monday of Week 4, before the Horns faced the Vols, Sarkisian expressed a similar sentiment, refusing to update members of the media on any lingering injuries, stating that "There's called an injury report in the SEC, so that's enough of the injury questions," Sarkisian said that week. Based on the final injury list from Texas's game against Tennessee, one could easily assume that Smothers will be good to go against the Oklahoma Sooners this weekend as the Horns prepare for the annual Red River Rivalry. The star running back was off the report just before kickoff and was seen on the sidelines in full pads, with his helmet on, but never entered the game against the Volunteers. However, when it comes to Terry and Townsend, your guess is as good as mine. Smothers is nursing a reported lower-leg injury suffered in practice, Townsend is healing up from a knee injury he sustained before Week 2's kickoff, Terry is recovering from a toe injury ahead of Week 2's game, Coleman hasn't played since Week 3, and Filsaime has yet to take the field this season. For right now, Texas fans (and Oklahoma fans) will have to wait to see what Texas's injury list looks like on Wednesday evening, because until then, Sarkisian is remaining tight-lipped about the health of his team. home.headline: Oklahoma vs Texas: Key players listed on Wednesday Availability report
home.blurb: Most notable is that the guy who was supposed to start at left tackle, Michael Fasusi, doesn't look like he'll be available again this week. He started for the Sooners against UTEP but has missed the last three games with a shoulder injury. Fasusi is doubtful for the Red River Showdown. Also in question is the status of starting left guard Eddy Pierre-Louis. Pierre-Louis was listed as questionable going into Saturday. Joining the ranks of the unavailable this week are Xavier Robinson and Jacobe Johnson. Johnson suffered an injury during the loss to Georgia. Why Robinson isn't available is anyone's guess. He didn't get much playing time against the Bulldogs, logging just three snaps after getting nine snaps the week before against Michigan. Along with Fasusi, who is doubtful, are reserve backup tight end Trynae Washington and backup offensive lineman Fred Hinton. Washington has been a piece of Oklahoma's short-yardage formations, lining up in the backfield as a fullback for the Sooners. Their presence on the availability report is just another week where the Sooners will have question marks along the offensive line. Names to watch as the week moves along include linebacker Cole Sullivan, wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, safety Michael Boganowski, and tight end Jack Van Dorselaer. The Sooners need a spark this week if they want to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. The Sooners are 1-3 against the Texas Longhorns under Brent Venables, and the offense hasn't scored a touchdown against their Red River rivals since 2023. Missing key members of the offensive line and the tight end room doesn't bode well for the Sooners' chances this Saturday. Even redshirt junior quarterback Dante Moore could rest some more after suffering a concussion in the victory at the USC Trojans on Sept. 26. He was at the first practice this week, wearing a helmet and shoulder pads, according to coach Dan Lanning. Moore's next possible opponent would be the No. 21 UCLA Bruins (4-0, 2-0 Big Ten) , who are one of the three remaining undefeated Big Ten Conference programs. The Ducks' moneyline is -480 and the Bruins' is +360. The over/under is set at 58.5. The last time these two former Pac-12 Conference opponents met was in 2024, resulting in a 34-13 victory for Oregon in Pasadena, California. Their running backs are as good as anyone who will go against them this year. They have a lot of players that came with them. And again, why I draw some comparisons to Indiana: a lot of guys that traveled with their coach right to the next stop.” First-year UCLA coach Bob Chesney brought offensive coordinator Dean Kennedy, defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler, and fifth-year running back Wayne Knight along with him to sunny California after the James Madison Dukes of the Sun Belt Conference made the College Football Playoff last season. Their memorable run came to an end in the first round after a 51-34 loss to the Ducks in the Pacific Northwest on Dec. 21, 2025. “Extremely well-coached team," Lanning continued on about this year's Bruins. "You got two coordinators who were with him before, so they've been together for a while. They have a lot of continuity from that standpoint. They're running the ball as well as anybody in college football.” Sep 12, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second half against San Diego State at the Rose Bowl. On Oct. 5, Lanning reiterated to the media just how effective Chesney's offense is without an efficient passing game. "I would argue they have explosive runs; anytime you can run the ball in the end zone, I think they have more rushing touchdowns this year than they've had in the last two years combined," stated Lanning. Knight is one of the top ball carriers in the nation. He has already collected 445 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns (tied for the third-most in the sport). Slowing the star back down is the key to an Oregon winning effort over that confident unit in the backfield. "Against the run, I think we do a good job stopping runs between the tackles," Lanning explained back on Sept. 30. "However, we give up some big runs around the outside, and we need to do a better job defending and adjusting to those plays." picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Picks UCLA vs. Oregon Winner With Dante Moore's Status Unclear Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy picked Oregon to beat unbeaten No. 21 UCLA on Saturday at Autzen Stadium, betting that the Ducks' run defense can contain first-year coach Bob Chesney's ground game whether Dante Moore or Dylan Raiola starts at quarterback. McElroy took the Ducks 31-21 on his Always College Football podcast and built the pick around a red-zone trend for Oregon coach Dan Lanning. "Dan Lanning is 39-1 in his career when Oregon gets more red-zone trips than the opponent," McElroy said. Who starts at quarterback for Oregon? Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola throws a pass as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Trojans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Raiola replaced Moore at the Coliseum and went 19 of 25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns. However, McElroy pointed to the Nebraska transfer's history against ranked teams. "If you look back at his time at Nebraska, he was 0-5 against ranked football teams," McElroy said. "Well, UCLA is ranked." A Raiola start would also come one week before Oregon faces Nebraska. Wayne Knight vs. Oregon run defense UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) looks on after scoring a touchdown during the second half against San Diego State | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 54-3 win at Maryland on Sept. 26. Chesney became the first UCLA coach since Red Sanders in 1949 to open his tenure 4-0 . UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 54-3 win at Maryland on Sept. 26. Chesney became the first UCLA coach since Red Sanders in 1949 to open his tenure 4-0 . Running back Wayne Knight, who followed Chesney from James Madison , has 445 yards and nine touchdowns on 49 carries against FBS opponents. McElroy noted the Bruins average 7 yards per carry, the best mark in the country. But Oregon has allowed just nine runs of 10 or more yards. The Bruins' passing game is the concern. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava has thrown four touchdown passes, which McElroy said ranks 118th nationally, and Chesney's teams struggle when they have to lean on the pass. "Bob Chesney is 20-1 as an FBS head coach when his team runs fewer than 30 pass plays," McElroy said. "He is 1-3 when they have to throw it 40 or more times." Why did McElroy pick Oregon? Oregon Ducks head coach Dan Lanning runs out to the field with players before a game against the Portland State Vikings | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. "Oregon will completely sell out against the run," McElroy said. "So once the Bruins are forced to throw the ball, that's when the matchup starts to tilt pretty hard in the direction of the Ducks," McElroy added. UCLA's best upset path runs through turnovers. The Bruins are plus-8 in turnover margin, tied for third nationally, while Oregon has given the ball away twice all season. UCLA also averages 10 penalties per game, which McElroy said ranks 137th out of 138 teams, and that number becomes harder to overcome in a road environment like Autzen. History favors the Ducks, too. Oregon has won the last five meetings, and McElroy noted UCLA's last win in Eugene came in 2004, when Lanning was a freshman linebacker at William Jewell. McElroy picked against Oregon in Week 4, taking USC 34-31 before the Ducks won by 14 at the Coliseum. UCLA and Oregon kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS. Loading recommendations...
