picks.headline: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown
picks.blurb: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers return to NLCS Rays sweep Yankees Brewers clinch NLCS Valkyries, Dream win Game 2s NFL Power Rankings Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks are in the midst of a much-needed bye week, enjoying some time off after a strenuous and pressure-filled first month of the 2026 season. Through four games, we've seen the Ducks start at No. 2 in the AP poll, drop to No. 6 after an underwhelming win over Boise State before losing to Oklahoma State, dropping them all the way down to No. 21. They then took care of Portland State, 84-0, moving them up a spot before a pivotal road matchup in Los Angeles with USC . The Ducks never blinked, even when quarterback Dante Moore had to leave the game via ambulance with a head injury, as backup Dylan Raiola and some timely defensive plays powered Oregon over USC, 41-27. It was as impressive of a win as we've seen from the Ducks over the past two seasons, and one that they badly needed in order to keep their goals of winning a national championship alive. Now, Oregon gets to take a breath and relax with a Week 5 bye. But that's not all that the players and staff are doing, as they'll be getting a jumpstart on preparing for the upstart UCLA Bruins , who will come to town in Week 6. We'll follow suit, providing an early deep-dive preview of how the Bruins ' season has gone so far, a breakdown of the offense, defense, special teams and players to watch with game and betting details to boot. Let's start with UCLA's resume, as they head into the matchup with Oregon looking to continue their undefeated season. UCLA's Resume Through Five Weeks Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins wide receiver Aidan Mizell (1) dances in the end zone with wide receiver Landon Ellis (11) and wide receiver Semaj Morgan (4) after catching an 83-yard touchdown reception in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Week 1: W 45-24 @ Cal Week 2: W 28-10 vs. San Diego State Week 3: W 52-38 vs. Purdue Week 4: W 52-3 @ Maryland The Bruins got off to an impressive start in the newly-hired Bob Chesney era, taking down the Tosh Lupoi-led Golden Bears on the road after a dominant second half. Chesney, who commanded James Madison to the College Football Playoff a year ago, relied upon several of his former Dukes that followed him to Westwood in the season-opener. The start of the season was strong, and so was last game for UCLA. The Bruins went into Maryland and stomped all over the Terrapins, picking off four passes and racking up 475 total yards. The early, 10:30 PT start didn't hold them back, as they jumped out to a 20-3 lead at halftime and only added to the lead after the break. Sandwiched between those two spectacular outings were victories over San Diego State and Purdue, with the offense carrying them in the former and offense in the latter, showing how well-rounded the Bruins are in 2026. Offensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins running back Jaivian Thomas (21) celebrates with offensive line Hall Schmidt (65) after scoring a touchdown in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images While last season was discombobulated at times for the Bruins offensively, new coordinator Dean Kennedy — coming over with Chesney from James Madison — has brought a revitalized, intelligent and, thus far, highly-successful offense to UCLA. Kennedy has a history of elevating previously subpar offensive units, as he developed quarterback Kyle Trask at Florida, turned Holy Cross into the Patriot League scoring leader and orchestrated the ninth-ranked scoring offense at James Madison in 2025. Now, he's doing the same thing at UCLA with a spread-based system that emphasizes physicality and explosiveness at the point of attack. Kennedy's units have consistently been among the best at creating explosive plays, both on the ground and through the air. While the Bruins won't go under center much at all, instead standing in the shotgun or pistol, they aren't afraid to run it right down the defense's throat. Through the air, the route combinations aren't necessarily complex, but they make it easy on the quarterback to read with a progression-based system. Defensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins linebacker Trent Hendrick (25) celebrates after intercepting a pass in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Also brought over from James Madison, Colin Hitschler is the defensive coordinator for the Bruins with a goal of instilling an uncommon physicality that hasn't been seen in Westwood for some time. And thus far this fall, UCLA has, for the most part, lived up those goals. The Bruins mostly operate out of a 4-2-5 defensive alignment, following the trend of opting to put an extra defensive back on the field over a lumbering linebacker. But make no mistake, the linebackers have plenty of talent to handle the middle of the field themselves, with a pair of seniors coming in at first and second on the team in tackles through four games. Hitschler isn't afraid to send pressure, having loads of success against Maryland in forcing the quarterback to make decisions under duress that turned into four interceptions. Expect more of the same come Week 6, with Hitschler putting the onus on the offensive line to protect whoever trots out at quarterback for the Ducks. Special Teams Breakdown Sep 12, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA kicker Mateen Bhaghani (15) kicks a field-goal during the second half against San Diego State at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images The Bruins have modest special teams units, with average kickoff and punt return marks with the same for the coverage units — though the return aspect could change in a blink with a pair of return men with elite speed waiting back there. In the kicking game, kicker Mateen Bhaghani has been solid in converting 4-of-5 field goals and all 23 extra points. It's his third season as the starter at UCLA, and he's made 82.8% of his field goals with a long of 57 yards — a massive advantage at the college level. Punter Curtis Gerrand also has a big leg, averaging 45.7 yards per punt on 15 boots thus far. Players to Watch Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava (9) passes in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images There's an abundance of talent across the roster, yet these three players will have to be accounted for by the Ducks if they're to get their fourth win. QB Nico Iamaleava 2026 Season Stats: 62-for-99, 820 yards, 4 TDs, 2 INTs / / 35 rushes, 143 yards, 1 TD Analysis: Iamaleava hasn't quite needed to show off his world-class athleticism this year, with his backfield mate stealing much of the thunder in the first month of the season. That's not to say the former Tennessee starter can't scoot, as he's run for 1,077 yards and 11 touchdowns in four seasons while tossing 38 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. Not the most refined passer, Iamaleava — like many college quarterbacks — feasts on short and long throws, but hasn't quite developed the intermediate aspect of his game. Still very talented, Iamaleava is commanding mid-to-late round draft buzz, though he does have one more season of eligibility remaining. RB Wayne Knight 2026 Season Stats: 49 rushes, 445 yards, 9 TDs / / 8 catches, 88 yards Analysis: Yes, you read that right. Wayne has nine touchdowns four games into the year, with six coming in the first two games. Standing just 5-foot-7 and 193 pounds, Knight makes up for his lack of size with elite speed, vision and playmaking ability. At James Madison in 2025, Knight broke off runs of 73, 59, 58 and 49 yards with 57 and 49-yard gains on receptions. Always an ability to hit a home-run, the Ducks will have to be cognizant not to lose Knight behind the Bruins' offensive line. LB Sammy Omosigho 2026 Season Stats: 37 tackles, 3 sacks, 4 forced fumbles Analysis: Though the Bruins added 2025 Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Year Trent Hendricks to the roster recently, he's still getting acclimated so we'll spotlight Sammy Omosigho here. The 6-foot-2, 239-pound four-year Oklahoma transfer has gotten off to a fast start at UCLA, leading the team in tackles and recording three sacks from his linebacker spot. Hitschler sends the former Sooner quite often on pressures and he makes plays as evidenced by his four forced fumbles in four games. picks.headline: 4 bold predictions as Oregon football looks for ranked win vs. UCLA
picks.blurb: News Sports Opinion Entertainment Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL 4 bold predictions as Oregon football looks for ranked win vs. UCLA Alec Dietz Eugene Register-Guard Updated Oct. 7, 2026, 12:40 p.m. PT Just two weeks following an emotional, gut-check win over USC in Los Angeles, the Oregon football team will look to take down UCLA on Oct. 10 in Eugene . The Ducks (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) were idle last week in their only bye of the season and take on a Bruins ' (4-0, 2-0) squad in the same position. "UCLA is playing a high level of ball," coach Dan Lanning said. "It's a coaching staff that we have a really high level of respect for." The game will kick off at 12:30 p.m. Saturday and air on CBS. Here's what to look for ahead of the ranked matchup. Oregon vs. UCLA scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: The Ducks are the only team in the country to average over 300 passing yards per game without an interception, split between starter Dante Moore and backup Dylan Raiola. Oregon ranks third nationally in passing yards per game and has done a good job of avoiding turnovers. If the Ducks can dictate tempo through the air, create explosive plays and avoid turnovers, they should win this game. Why UCLA has an advantage: The Bruins, to this point in the season, have run the ball much more consistently than the Ducks. UCLA ranks in the top five nationally in rush yards per play, rushing touchdowns and rushing yards per game. Led by standout back Wayne Knight, the Bruins average nearly 7 yards per carry. The Ducks rank toward the back half in the country around 4.6 yards per rushing attempt. If the Bruins can establish their ground game and control the tempo of this game, they'll have a chance to spring an upset. Oregon vs. UCLA injury updates For Oregon: The main storyline for the Ducks this week will likely be the health of starting quarterback. After suffering a concussion against USC, Moore returned to practice this week, but his status moving forward is unclear. Oregon's first mandatory injury report will be released Wednesday night and should offer clarity on his availability moving forward. Elsewhere, receiver Jeremiah McClellan is expected to be out still while Jalen Lott could make his return after a hand surgery sidelined him through Oregon's first four games. For UCLA: The Bruins' injury report will also be released Wednesday night, but several banged-up players made their returns in UCLA's last outing against Maryland in Week 4. Receiver Aidan Mizell, DB Jhase McMillan and tight end Josh Phifer were all listed as questionable or probable and shifted to available on game day. Safety Tao Johnson, a starter, could make his return after an upper-body injury in Week 1. Oregon vs. UCLA: 4 bold predictions Oregon needs to run the ball, much better than it has, to win Outside of a record-breaking outing against a completely outclassed opponent in Portland State, the Ducks haven't run the ball nearly as well as they typically have under Lanning. If you take out Oregon's 84-0 win over PSU, it is only rushing for roughly 115 yards per game, which would rank near the bottom of the country. The Bruins are one of the top rushing teams in the country. Though Oregon's offense has been able to move the ball effectively through the air, it will absolutely need to run the ball better than it has to beat the Bruins. Quarterback play will determine winner Through four games, Oregon's quarterback play has not been a major issue. Moore has been effective and avoided turnovers while Raiola stepped in masterfully to deliver a satisfying win over USC. That, obviously, needs to continue this Saturday, but the play of UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava might just determine how this game plays out. The previously maligned former five-star quarterback had a season to forget in 2025 but has been more effective in 2026. Still, the emphasis for Oregon all week will be on stopping the run, meaning Iamaleava will have opportunities to make plays throughout the game. If he can take advantage and outduel whoever starts at QB for Oregon, UCLA will be in the driver's seat to win. Oregon will play its best game of the season vs. UCLA Though the Ducks are 3-1, Lanning himself admitted during the bye week that they are nowhere near where they want to be. USC was a big step forward in multiple facets, but the defense has some lingering issues and the offense still has things to figure out. Saturday's game will be Oregon's best effort of the season, following a recalibrating bye week. Still feeling the urgency from the Oklahoma State loss in Week 2, getting back in front of fans at Autzen Stadium will energize the Ducks, who will roar out to a double-digit win this Saturday in Eugene. away.blurb: Dante Moore injury update: Oregon QB ruled out of Saturday's showdown vs. UCLA - CBS Sports site: media | arena: collegefootball | pageType: stories | section: | slug: dante-moore-injury-explaining-the-ncaas-concussion-protocol-and-if-oregon-qb-can-play-vs-ucla | sport: collegefootball | route: article_single.us | 6-keys: media/spln/collegefootball/reg/free/stories Skip to Main Content Close Menu All Sports Menu Sports Watch Fantasy Betting Featured NFL User Menu Settings Log Out Log In Sign Up Fantasy & Games See All ArrowForward # # LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Getty Images Oregon quarterback Dante Moore has been ruled out for the Ducks game against UCLA, the team announced in its injury report on Wednesday evening. Oregon coach Dan Lanning said last Saturday on "Big Noon Kickoff" that the program is exercising an "abundance of caution" and there's no timetable for his return, emphasizing there is no rush in his recovery. "Similar to what we said before, we're gonna do what's best for Dante moving forward," Lanning reiterated in his Monday press conference. "It was great to see him back out there with his teammates getting to work today." The team physician determines "pre-participation clearance and/or the need for additional consultation or testing." The NCAA mandates that when an athlete shows signs of a concussion, they are not allowed to return to the game. The NCAA's concussion safety protocol management guidelines state that a player's return to play is a step-by-step process that must be completed without symptoms returning -- almost like weather delays, when a single streak of lightning in the area delays a return to action. The five stages of an athlete's return to play via the NCAA are as follows: Stage 1: Symptom-limited activity: Begin with light aerobic exercise. Stage 5: Return to competition: An athlete can return to game play only after successfully completing all prior stages and receiving medical clearance. With Monday's return to practice, the next update from Lanning and the Ducks' coaching staff on Moore comes later this week. Given Moore's status and Raiola's play off the bench, Lanning has a difficult choice on who to play in the coming weeks if his starter is ready to return to action. Raiola completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, executing Oregon's offense to near perfection in the second half of the win over the Trojans. This comes after the Ducks had looked out of rhythm several times in the early going this fall, following a near-stumble against Boise State and a loss at Oklahoma State. The Ducks' secondary depth may be limited, with two defensive backs listed as doubtful. Moore, who suffered a concussion and had to be taken off the field in an ambulance in the first half of the Ducks ' Sept. 26 game against USC, was officially listed as "out" on Oregon's Big Ten-mandated availability report that was released Wednesday. Wide receivers Jeremiah McClellan and Jack Ressler, offensive lineman Trent Ferguson, inside linebacker Brayden Platt, and running back Simeon Price were also listed as out. Oregon's secondary depth also could be thin on Saturday as starting safety Aaron Flowers and reserve cornerback Aaron Scott Jr. were both listed as doubtful. With Moore out, the Ducks will turn to Dylan Raiola, a former 23-game starter at Nebraska who had an impressive outing against the Trojans when Moore got hurt. Raiola threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns on 19-of-25 passing in the USC win . Tony Cumberland – The four-star freshman defensive tackle from Eugene's Willamette High School was injured in an offseason car accident and remains out. "It's a work in progress with him," Oregon defensive line coach Tony Tuioti said Aug. 17. "I don't think it's going to be anything that we'll be able to see him soon. But he's made so much progress. I think the thing that's most important is that we have him with us and just having him in the room brings a smile to all our faces." "It was great to see him back out there with his teammates getting to work today." The team physician determines "pre-participation clearance and/or the need for additional consultation or testing." The NCAA mandates that when an athlete shows signs of a concussion, they are not allowed to return to the game. The NCAA's concussion safety protocol management guidelines state that a player's return to play is a step-by-step process that must be completed without symptoms returning -- almost like weather delays, when a single streak of lightning in the area delays a return to action. The five stages of an athlete's return to play via the NCAA are as follows: Stage 1: Symptom-limited activity: Begin with light aerobic exercise. Stage 5: Return to competition: An athlete can return to game play only after successfully completing all prior stages and receiving medical clearance. With Monday's return to practice, the next update from Lanning and the Ducks' coaching staff on Moore comes later this week. Raiola completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, executing Oregon's offense to near perfection in the second half of the win over the Trojans. home.blurb: On Wednesday night, the first availability report of the week was released, and Kentucky has a multitude of players listed on it. The biggest news comes at linebacker, where Alex Afari is still ineligible, and both Tavion Wallace and Antwan Smith listed as out. That leaves starters Grant Godfrey and Bo Barnes healthy, but not much experience behind them. Defensive back Jaden Smith is also listed as out. There is good news for the Wildcats. Wide receiver D.J. Miller is listed as probable, and they'll be happy to have him back. With Nic Anderson fresh off a breakout game, and the continued rise of Kenny Darby, Miller gives them a trio of receivers who won't allow the LSU defense to double team the tight ends. The Kentucky football team takes the field on Saturday in their biggest test of the year so far. They'll take on Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers who are ranked No. 10 in the country. In addition, they'll do so short-handed, especially at the linebacker position. On the LSU side, the biggest loss is tight end Trey'Dez Green. They'll also be without a pair of linebackers in starter Whit Weeks and backup Charles II. Going into such a big game without some key players is tough, but it's a part of the game. Will Stein and Jay Bateman will have to hope no further injuries occur, and that Godfrey and Barnes are ready for a heavy workload. picks.blurb: Georgia vs. Alabama Odds See Notable Shift With Weather Potentially Impacting Week 6 Matchup Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Week 6 of the college football season features a massive SEC matchup between the No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs and the No. 6 Alabama Crimson Tide. However, the weather may take center stage with Tropical Storm Isaias potentially impacting the region ahead of Saturday's 7:30 p.m. EST kickoff. Alabama released a statement about the forecast ahead of Saturday's game, and it's possible that it could get moved if the storm becomes a major issue. For now, kickoff remains the same time on Saturday night. Information on Saturday’s Alabama football game vs. Georgia #RollTide | @AlabamaFTBL pic.twitter.com/KteQ9GgBZ6 Oddsmakers have already altered the odds for this game in a big way since they opened with Georgia favored by 2.5 points on Sunday. The total was originally 56.5 for this rivalry game, but that has come down considerably with the weather potentially playing a factor on Saturday. On Wednesday, DraftKings Sportsbook has the Crimson Tide set as 1.5-point favorites at home (a four-point swing in the odds) while the total has dropped four points all the way down to 52.5. This is a huge change for the opening numbers, and it's a sign that weather could impact how well these teams can move the ball on Saturday. Earlier this week, I shared why I'm taking Alabama and Keelon Russell to win this matchup, and I still lean that way even if Tropical Storm Isaias plays a factor: With Russell really turning a corner over the last few weeks, Alabama is now ninth in the country in EPA/Pass this season. Overall, the Crimson Tide are No. 2 in the country in net adjusted EPA/Play. There is an experience advantage for Georgia with Stockton under center, but this Alabama team has turned in four consecutive wins over quality teams in Kentucky, South Carolina, Florida State and Mississippi State. The Crimson Tide are No. 1 in the country in offensive success rate and No. 20 in defensive success rate, holding three of the four Power Four teams that they’ve played to 23 or fewer points. I think Alabama is going to be able to move the ball through the air against this Georgia team, and the Bulldogs haven’t been tested yet against an offense of this caliber. There's a chance the odds for this game could shift even more throughout the week, and the total would likely change if the game is pushed to a new time -- or even a different day -- to avoid this storm. For now, Alabama has a slight edge in what may be a low-scoring matchup on Saturday. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Alabama's first-year starter has been excellent lately, with 13 touchdowns and no turnovers in his last three games. However, those games came against Florida State, South Carolina, and Mississippi State. Georgia allows just 57.4 rushing yards per game, third-best in the country. If that holds, Alabama's offense will rest almost entirely on Russell's arm. On the other side, Gunner Stockton is a fifth-year senior. He's 17-3 as a starter, 6-2 against ranked teams, and third nationally in passing efficiency at 202.0. He gets an Alabama pass defense that allows 234 yards per game , ranking 14th in the SEC. Stockton also protects the ball: he has just eight interceptions in 571 career attempts . That matters against a Tide defense that leads the SEC with 13 takeaways. Georgia usually starts fast, outscoring opponents 70-7 in the first quarter. That's a problem for Alabama, because Kalen DeBoer is 1-7 at Alabama when trailing at halftime. Yes, Kirby Smart is 0-7 against Alabama in the regular season, and DeBoer is 16-1 at Bryant-Denny. But the last time these teams met, Georgia won the SEC title game 28-7. Steam is coming out of their ears. They are irate because the Alabama dynasty is not dead and they actually have to write good things about the Crimson Tide. Alabama (5-0) has run roughshod over their competition. The Tide has averaged 49.6 point per game and no game has been below 45 points in scoring for Bama. The Bulldogs have had a simpler schedule but have had similar results. UGA has averaged 51.4 ppg but the last two games have been 41 and 38 points scored. In short, these two teams score a good deal of points. In the preseason, Georgia was a FanDuel +2.5 favorite over Alabama. But much has changed and the the script has flipped. FanDuel now has opening odds of Alabama being a 1.5 point favorite over the Bulldogs with an Over/Under of 55.5 . So far this season, the sportsbooks have pegged UGA with healthy point spreads as well as decent sized Over/Under in each game. However ,most of them have been too low. Much like Alabama, the Vegas bookies have been giving UGA some pretty low numbers. They covered the spread and went over the points total in each of their first four games. This past weekend was the first bucking of that trend as the Doggies did not cover and had their lowest points total of the young season. In preseason, many observers figured Oklahoma would be a tougher competition. But who knew John Mateer would be such dog poo and gift the Bulldogs so many points? It is a mystery why anyone thinks a post-Diego Pavia Vanderbilt would be anything worth worrying about. Arkansas is in a deep funk. All that said, Georgia really has not played anyone worth a hill o' beans. To date, UGA opponents are collectively 9-15. Their Strength of Schedule is 97th. Alabama foes are 15-9. The Tide SOS is 23rd. The Las Vegas guys have underestimated the Tide all season. The Bama Boys have been killing the Over/Unders and had only one misstep against the spread. It was mentioned in this space last weak that perhaps the FSU game was a fluke. Upon further reflection, it might just be the rapid pace that Bama QB Keelon Russell is developing and improving. The Tide offense is stacking up some points. Georgia and Alabama are No. 1 and 3 respectively in scoring in FBS thus far this season. The Bulldogs are putting up 51.4 ppg but that number is skewed by the 70-burger they put up on woeful WKU (1-4) who yielded 49 to Nevada. This Bama-UGA game will be the game of the week under a lot of spotlights. It will be the secondAlabama night game following the South Carolina match-up. Early forecasts are calling for rain in Tuscaloosa on Saturday. But that is what they were saying about the MSU game as well. With an over/under of 55.5 and 1.5 point spread by FanDuel , the final score could look something like Bama 29-27 or so. Does that seem logical? Once again, I am going over on both of these lines. Both defenses for these teams are better than either has faced, but it just feels like both teams will go over 30 points with the Tide winning by 5 or so. What do you think? Alabama will be hosting the Bulldogs in the game, offering them a slight advantage coming into the contest. But this game will be anything but a bloodbath, with both sides desperately wanting to win. Each team enters this matchup with a record of 5-0, going 3-0 in SEC play so far this season. The two rivals have continuously given fans epic games over the years, and this matchup should be no different. Alabama comes in ranked No. 6 in the country, while Georgia is No. 2. For the Crimson Tide, they have a chance to take down one of the top teams in the nation at home, helping their own resume in the process. Entering the game, the matchup looks pretty even, with both teams having a real chance to take home the win. But according to ESPN's game predictor , Alabama has a slightly bigger opportunity to get the victory. Alabama has been given a 52.6 percent chance to take down Georgia, showing some of the slimmest of margins coming into the game. Part of why the Crimson Tide may be favored here is because the game is being played in Tuscaloosa. The Crimson Tide are very tough to beat at home, but Georgia is one of the few teams that has the talent to make it happen. Alabama will need to make sure that they bring their A-game into this matchup; otherwise, it could be a long night for everyone involved. Quarterback Keelon Russell is going to be tested in ways that he hasn't been so far this season, and he will need to prove that he can step up for the team. For Alabama to reach its big goals of winning a title this year, Russell is going to have to take on teams like Georgia while performing at a high level. But so far this year, Russell has passed all his tests with flying colors, entering his name into the Heisman Trophy conversation . If Russell can have another strong game against the Bulldogs, Alabama would likely be put in a good spot to grab the win at home. This is a measuring stick game for both teams, and the winner will have the upper hand to get into the College Football Playoff . Kickoff for this game will take place at 4:30 p.m. PT/7:30 p.m. ET from Bryant-Denny Stadium.

Alabama is coming off arguably their most impressive performance of the season. The Tide destroyed Mississippi State, 56-23, never trailing in the game. Alabama outgained Mississippi State in yards 483-302, went 6-of-9 on third downs, and forced four turnovers (2 INT, 2 Fumbles). Keelon Russell had another dominant outing with 301 total yards and four touchdowns (3 pass, 1 rush). Russell is climbing the Heisman Trophy rankings and a win over Georgia would likely jolt him to the top spot. Alabama has owned the series against Georgia winning 10 of the past 12, but the Bulldogs won the previous matchup 28-7. The Bulldogs haven't been tested much yet so far this year, but that's likely to change on Saturday against an explosive Crimson Tide offensive attack. Recently, college football media personality Josh Pate dropped a hot take in anticipation of the big matchup. "It's game of the year potential. It's not the end of the world for the loser. This season's guest pickers have featured the likes of Morgan Freeman and Lainey Wilson. While it is anyone's guess, here are five options for the GameDay guest picker in Tuscaloosa this Saturday. Young also has history with Georgia, having played against the Bulldogs in the 2021 SEC Championship Game in which he threw for 421 yards, as well as the 2021 CFP national championship. Jones also has history with Georgia as he went for five catches, 94 yards, and a touchdown in Alabama's 41-30 win over Georgia in the infamous Georgia blackout game in Athens during his freshman season in 2008. Jones is also set to feature in the Nick Saban documentary that ESPN is putting out, of which the first episode of is set to be released on Thursday . Justin Thomas, pro golfer Sep 27, 2026; Medinah, Illinois, USA; Justin Thomas of the U.S. Team watches his birdie putt on the 15th green after putting to win his match during the final round of the Presidents Cup. Thomas was on the golf team at Alabama for two years, where he helped lead Alabama to a national championship in 2013, before turning pro. home.headline: Penn State Week 6 Injury Report: Latest Updates, Replacement Options vs. USC
home.blurb: Penn State released its first availability report Wednesday ahead of the White Out game vs. USC, which included a few familiar names on questionable list. The Nittany Lions host the Trojans on Saturday night at Beaver Stadium in a game with several fascinating storylines . Two defensive players listed as questionable Penn State listed linebacker Alex Tatsch and defensive lineman Armstrong Nnodim as questionable on Wednesday's availability report. Both players returned from prior injuries this season. Penn State already is without linebacker Cam Smith, out for his fifth straight game, and needs Tatsch in the rotation. The position is thin behind Rojas already. It's a good sign that Penn State center Brock Riker is not listed on the availability report, but he still hasn't been healthy since the Temple game. He played just two series the following week against Buffalo, ceding the position to Vaea Ikakoula, but and was listed as probable before the Big Ten opener against Wisconsin. "[Riker] has been gutting it out the last couple of weeks," Campbell said. "Taking care of him in the last quarter, getting an extra day [by playing Friday], I certainly think he's been a lot better. It's something that's not 100 percent, [but he's] working to get back. He's a lot closer this week than he has been the last couple of weeks." Koby Howard out for third straight week Koby Howard, who still leads Penn State in receiving yards despite playing just three games, will miss his third Big Ten game this weekend. Campbell also popped the optimism balloon that Howard might return against Michigan on Oct. 17, saying the receiver is "a couple weeks away" from playing. Could USC get electric receiver Trent Mosley back for Saturday? The freshman is listed as questionable after missing the last three games. Mosley went from questionable to doubtful to out before USC's game last week against Washington. Mosley began the season with back-to-back 100-yard receiving games against San Jose State and Fresno State. Mosley also is a weapon on special teams, averaging 31.6 yards per punt return. He has been out since getting injured in the Trojans' third game against Louisiana. Tight end Mark Bowman also is listed as questionable after missing last week's game against Washington. Bowman ranks second on the team in receptions (21) and has scored two touchdowns. Elsewhere, USC left tackle Hayden Treter is questionable, as is defensive tackle Jahkeem Stewart, who recovered a strip-sack fumble against Washington and returned it for a touchdown.
